summary:
Building a survival and resource management game taking place on the moon with an extension bay to remotely conduct a mission on Mars, the gameplay loop is you are the team leader managing your team and project goals you end each day by going to a panel that views all available team in a meeting where you can choose if you want to send someone on an expedition on maintenance or have something process overnight and said actions translate to the next day, core mechanics so far are: managing power and oxygen choosing what tasks to do knowing it will have to use that sacrifices something else they are like the main trading system in the game, buggy communication with home managing going no contact due to errors n such, Radiation exposure: how will you maintain the shields? What if an astronaut gets infected? What if a leak happens??, managing resources you took from earth knowing you will likely not get any new ones swell as managing food production, and lastly keeping in mind each action affects the outcome in a way negatively or postivily, but to keep young players engaged the game also includes world building each astronauts has their own silly perks and stories, and you can do many activities to keep moral up like boardgames or chitchatting game also includes up beat background noises swell as silly eastereggs to keep players engaged mixing fun with learning

details:
1.basic info 2.challenges and their mechanics 3.gameplay loop in detail 4.process of making the outpost map in detail 5.how we optimised the game to keep all ages entertained RPG-based resource management game. It was created by Godot using GDscript. While the demo algorithms are tested using Python, all assets were created on Kriya or got from open source on itch.io, the game runs on a day-by-day system and several algorithms are used to run all the processes. The main game loop is you play as the leader of the first ever fully optimised space outpost with 3 astronauts. Each astronaut has their own personality to keep the player entertained and to make the game feel more alive and the consequences more real. The game has you manage several challenges (will explain each in detail) with a new challenge getting introduced every day. For the first 7 days, any other challenge is optionally unlocked by the player (will explain in detail), with the addition of mentor bonus notes and tips sometimes The first challenge is managing the astronauts, their roles, jobs, physical and mental health, etc . . .. The first challenge is that hunger food is extremely limited in space, especially in an outpost of such a location. As a leader, you must manage the resources according to supply and demand. What food will your team eat? Can you afford to make one skip a meal for the day? Who will eat quality food for the day? (which ties back to the mental health mechanic explained in a second). Each astronaut starts with 100% hunger. In normal circumstances, they will steadily lose 15% of their hunger every day. Abnormal circumstances include: an astronaut who is sent on an expedition depending on how far they have gone and how many days they will lose hunger. According to the equation: 3% * distance in km * (1/6) (3% typical percentage multiply the distance and multiply 1 over 6 the difference between earth and moon), another abnormal circumstance is the atsronouts mental state. It is a direct relationship with hunger. The less happy an astronaut is, the faster they lose hunger The second challenge is deciding who to give what role every day. Every astronomer has their own perks and rebuffs, and you have to keep all of them in mind. For example: this astronaut is perfect at maintaining the greenhouse, but they are fast too, and I need to send an explanation. Can I afford to sacrifice some crop and lose the astronaut for multiple days for the sake of the mission? A huge challenge related to roles is: who can take the day off? Can I afford to not only lose workforce but also lose power and o2 to give them a source of entertainment? Which brings us to the biggest challenge: power and oxygen supply, dots like the currency in our game. Every discussion and every action affects these two variables, which gets tricky because, for example, are you ready to sac a lot of power for the chance of your nuclear experiment to work and produce power? Now, to keep things fun and fresh, after all, this is for young minds, we introduced a visitor mechanic. Every few days, you get knocks on your outpost from strangers, astronauts from short missions, missing astronauts lost in space, grace from a project, hail Merry, even an alien for the fans. If you have to keep it academic, each guest comes with risks: diseases, food etc. Now these are only the main challenges. Depending on the level and difficulty, more are added, like radiation risks and infection and moon dust debris etc. Now for the mechanics, The main mechanic is the daily system inspired by games like 60 seconds and Minecraft combined. You go on your day doing puzzles and mini-games and reading fun facts of the day, and end the day by approaching the table in the central doc. Once opened, a screen gets opened to your inventory, important calendar events and astronauts. It is here where you give yourself food and items and assign roles, then end the day. The calendar system: every few days a mentor that looks suspiciously alien (you're not allowed to ask questions at the central hub at home says she's human) and with news like: moon dust storm in X days, cargo shipment in X days, power outage, eclipse, etc. Food mechanic: We decided to combine the pre-existing mechanics in spaceships with the proposed mechanism of green houses. Success rates in the pre-existing chambers are much higher, but with fewer quantities and variety, while green households have much more crops, they are more prone to failure and the probability of success increases as more research is done. Getting water is done by expeditions to the dark sides of the moon collecting frozen ice. The map: Central hub: where the day starts and ends, only holds this mechanic Garden chambers: you enter room 1, which includes the classic planning system and a door with a screen to view the greenhouse and your inventory. It holds custom up to show how many plants are ready to harvest and their qualities (kinda like Star dew Valley). It also holds chambers in the walls to store water packs. Crew quarters: two-story sections. The floor contains the common areas, the exercise room and the activities' hub. Here is where you will find astronauts you sent on a day off during the day cycle, either knitting, playing games, watching TV, reading or playing board games. If the game reads more than one astronaut with a day off. The second floor contains the chambers, since this is a long-term outpost. The rooms are slightly bigger and more personalised with posters, plush and photos. Each chamber holds a combacxt phone booth shaped room with a bed and a sliceable table and personal comms, The kitchen: bigger than other chambers as it includes the dining area and preparation station. It includes a heater and a hydration bay as well as all the food, mainly shelves of packed dehydrated food in bags and containers like beans and such. The kitchen also includes boxes of special items sent by astronauts' family members and includes a small room full of all food storage. Research labs: divided into 5 sections: main bay where meetings can be held, room1: organic matter testing room, room2: Mars observation hub where they watch and study rovers sent on Mars remotely, room3: life support/hospital, room4: vehicle testing hub Control zone: main comms section with earth, tutorial and mentor Tutorial system: The first week is where essential mechanics get introduced. day1: main game mechanism, power trading system, research points and consequences day2: fresh food mechanics and gardening (basically only green houses are unlocked at high research points) day3: mental health mechanism day4: radiation and environmental prevention and maintenance day5: Mars study mechanics day5: power generation system day6: the guests/ visitors mechanism day7: expeditions on a larger scale Finally, to keep players entertained, we adopted soft colours and fun-eaters eggs as well as personalities and interests in each astronaut.
